prerequisites: Ability to analyze and structure simple interactive applications.
Expertise gained in foundational courses helps to understand the development logic of interactive and multimedia environments.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with theoretical and practical skills in the development of interactive digital content using Unity.
Provide students with the knowledge and skills needed to create interactive digital content, virtual 2D and 3D environments, and simple multimedia applications using the Unity game engine.

Enable students to apply their knowledge and understanding in evaluating development tools for interactive prototyping, implementing game logic and dynamic elements through Unity scripting, organizing project structures, and optimizing functionality for standard devices (desktop and mobile).

Select the most effective strategies for designing interactive environments aligned with project goals, choose the most suitable approaches among various programming, layout, and interaction solutions, and critically assess the outcomes of their implementations.

Clearly articulate design choices, techniques used, and functionalities developed in projects, and enhance the ability to produce technical documentation and present work through intuitive interfaces and visual feedback.

Integrate the knowledge gained in other courses with advanced digital tools for multimedia content creation, independently explore new Unity features and support libraries, and investigate emerging technologies in creative and interactive domains, presenting concise and effective summaries of their results.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course and development environment (2 hours)
Fundamentals of scripting and gameplay (10 hours)
bibliography: Joseph Hocking, Unity in Action, Third Edition: Multiplatform game development in C#, Manning, 2022.
